title: Developer - SD Specialty
description: Real-time streaming data integration with Pentaho Data Integration. Consume and process unbounded event streams over MQTT, AMQP, and Apache Kafka — IoT sensor telemetry, message-queue pipelines, and real-time user-activity streams using Pentaho Data Integration's parent/child streaming pattern.

assistant.subject: streaming data pipelines in PDI (MQTT, AMQP and Kafka consumers, brokers and message processing)
suggestions: What is the difference between MQTT, AMQP and Kafka?
How does the MQTT consumer step hand records to a child transformation?
Why does my consumer step need a batch size or duration?
How do I check what a broker received without Pentaho Data Integration?

moduleSummaries.title: Getting Started
moduleSummaries.summary: How to get the most out of this guide, and how to set your machine up — Podman Desktop, one command for all four brokers (HiveMQ, EMQX, RabbitMQ, Kafka), and Python for the publisher scripts.

moduleSummaries.title: Streaming Data
moduleSummaries.summary: Process unbounded, real-time event streams with Pentaho Data Integration's streaming steps. Batch versus streaming, the parent/child transformation pattern, and the Get records from stream step that underpins every streaming source.

moduleSummaries.title: MQTT
moduleSummaries.summary: Message Queuing Telemetry Transport — the lightweight publish/subscribe protocol for IoT. Two workshops: industrial robot-sensor telemetry via a HiveMQ broker, and a delivery-truck predictive-maintenance use case via an EMQX broker.

moduleSummaries.title: AMQP
moduleSummaries.summary: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol — reliable, decoupled messaging via exchanges, bindings, and queues. Workshop: consume room-sensor data from a RabbitMQ broker with the AMQP consumer step and append it to a text file.

moduleSummaries.title: Kafka
moduleSummaries.summary: Apache Kafka — a distributed event-streaming platform running in KRaft mode. Workshop: consume a real-time user-activity stream with the Kafka consumer step and load it into a MySQL warehouse.

moduleSummaries.title: Capstone Project
moduleSummaries.summary: One project across the course: three machines over MQTT with one wildcard subscription, every reading archived, alerts published to a keyed Kafka topic, and a consumer group that loads them into MySQL exactly once.
